title: Drop a motorized roller's hex ends point-up into its frame slots without pulling its cable, then fit its torque plate
keywords: shaft clocking inside a turning tube
instruction: Seat the roller's hex ends point-up in the frame slots without pulling its cable, then drop the torque plate over the hex.
context: Building a mobile robot's conveyor module: a 24 V motorized roller's two hex shaft ends drop blind into the frame slots at once, point-up. The motor sits on the fixed shaft and the tube turns round it, so the hex is clocked at the shaft while its short cable stays slack; a torque plate then locks the hex.
setup: Positions in cm from the arm bases' midpoint (x forward, y left), heights above the table. Frame: dark blue aluminium rails 17 x 0.6 x 7.5 tall, x 21.5 to 38.5, inside faces at y +-11.8, each with an open-top slot at x 30, 1.3 wide, down to a 120 deg V seat 4.4 up. Left rail outer face at x 30: plate guide posts at x 27.2-28.0 and 32.0-32.8 (2.8 to 7.0 up) with front lips, over a ledge 2.8 up; green driver-card box 6 x 2.2 x 3.2 at x 20.5-26.5, y 12.4-14.6. Roller along y at x 16.5, axis 3.9 up, tube on two grey 90 deg V blocks (6 x 1.6 x 2.8) at y +-7.5: a steel shaft 28.0 long (11 mm hex stub 2.75 long at each end, flats on top; 0.40 kg with motor) inside a zinc-plated steel tube 3.8 OD x 22.5 (0.30 kg) that turns on it. A black 0.6 OD cable, 18.0 long, runs from the left shaft end out to y 21.5, back along x to a fixed connector at x 23.5, y 15-17. Torque plate: 4 mm SUS304, 3.4 x 7.0, 72 g, bottom notch with a point-up 120 deg apex, upright in a grey rack at x 35.5, y 21.5.
scoring: At the end, both grippers open. Score 0 if the cable was ever pulled straight (span from connector to shaft end over 95% of its 18.0 cm length for 0.25 s or more; real trial: 17.1 cm or more on a tape, from video), or if it ends between the rails, in a slot or in the plate pocket. Otherwise 0.25 when both hex stubs sit in their slots: axes within 0.15 cm of the seat height (5.0 up) and 0.2 cm of the slot centre line, each hex stub over at least 0.2 cm of its own 0.6 cm rail, level within 3 deg; +0.25 when also the hex is point-up within 5 deg (angle gauge on an end flat; read on the shaft, not the tube); +0.25 when also the torque plate is down in its guide over the hex (notch apex within 0.15 cm of its seat and 0.3 cm of the slot line, upright within 10 deg); +0.25 when also both hands are 3 cm clear of the roller, cable and plate. Scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Put the plate back in its rack and the roller on the V blocks, turn the shaft by its right hex stub until a flat is on top (the tube may turn with it), and lay the cable along its taped outline. The cable stays attached at both ends.
fidelity: Full size. The shaft (hex stubs, motor and gearbox, 0.40 kg) is one body, the end of a 9-link cable chain anchored at its connector; the 0.30 kg tube rides on a sleeve keyed to it (0.5 mm play) and turns on it against 0.10 N m drag plus 0.1 N m s/rad damping (design values). The cable is limp: elastic to 3 deg per joint, then it keeps its bend. A pull is its span reaching 95%. Slots, V seats and plate notch are contact geometry.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (Moved arms back and away, roller stayed on its blocks, plate stayed in rack); demo: 1 (Right arm set the roller in the frame slots, left arm dropped the plate, both withdrew)
